title: The closure-normalized relative transpose agrees with the ambient immersion transpose
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $s:S\hookrightarrow T$ be an immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, factored as $s=v\circ c$ with $c:S\hookrightarrow V$ closed and $v:V\hookrightarrow T$ open [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the two small sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Put $F_\tau=v_{\tau,!}c_{\tau,*}$ and $J_\tau=Rc_\tau^!v_\tau^*$ for $\tau=e,p$, with the pasted adjunctions $F_\tau\dashv J_\tau$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient, lem-exc-proetale-closed-support, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], where the two open extensions are those of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Let $\bar S$ be the scheme-theoretic closure of $s$, with $s=i\circ u$, $u:S\hookrightarrow\bar S$ open and $i:\bar S\hookrightarrow T$ closed [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Here $\bar S=\operatorname{SIm}(s)$ is the closed subscheme cut out by the largest quasi-coherent ideal contained in $\ker(\mathcal O_T\to s_*\mathcal O_S)$; $i$ is its image inclusion and $u$ its canonical factor map. These immersions into the Noetherian scheme $T$ are quasi-compact, so this ideal is the kernel itself. Write $E_\tau=i_{\tau,*}u_{\tau,!}$.

Let $q_\tau:F_\tau\xrightarrow{\sim}E_\tau$ be the identity-normalized termwise extension identifications [lem-sfb-etale-locally-closed-extension-comparison, lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence], and identify $J_e$ with the etale compact-support right adjoint $s^\times$ by the adjunction conjugate of $q_e$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Write $C_W=\nu_W^*$ and $U_W=R\nu_{W,*}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], with unit $\eta_W$ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], and $G_s=C_Ss^\times U_T$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. For $L\in D^+(S_e,A)$ let
$$\Delta_L=v_{p,!}(\delta_{c,L})o_{v,c_{e,*}L},\qquad B_L=i_{p,*}(o_{u,L})\delta_{i,u_{e,!}L}$$
use the canonical counit-mate closed comparison and open comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. Suppose $q_{p,C_SL}\Delta_L=B_LC_T(q_{e,L})$ for every such $L$.

Let $M\in D^b_c(T_e,A)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] with $H=J_eM\in D^+(S_e,A)$. Suppose a natural isomorphism $\gamma_M:C_SH\xrightarrow{\sim}J_pC_TM$ satisfies
$$\epsilon^p_{C_TM}F_p(\gamma_M)\Delta_H=C_T(\epsilon^e_M),$$
where $\epsilon^\tau$ are the pasted counits. For every $h:F_pC_SL\to C_TM$, there is a unique $h_0:F_eL\to M$ with $h\Delta_L=C_T(h_0)$. Put $g_0=\operatorname{adj}_e(h_0):L\to H$ and $\rho_M=C_S(s^\times(\eta_{T,M}))$, under the fixed identification $J_e\cong s^\times$. Then
$$\operatorname{adj}_{F_p\dashv J_p}(h)=\gamma_MC_S(g_0),\qquad
\Phi_{L,C_TM}(h q_{p,C_SL}^{-1})=\rho_MC_S(g_0),$$
where $\Phi$ is the chosen-closure-compactification Hom bijection of [lem-pur-bounded-site-adjunction-transpose, thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. More explicitly, for $z:E_pC_SL\to C_TM$ this normalization is
$$\Phi_{L,C_TM}(z)=C_S\left(\operatorname{adj}_{E_e\dashv s^\times}\left(U_T(zB_L)\eta_{T,E_eL}\right)\right).$$
Consequently $\theta_M=\rho_M\gamma_M^{-1}:J_pC_TM\xrightarrow{\sim}G_s(C_TM)$ identifies the ambient and comparison-class Hom bijections, hence all their defined unit and counit maps. The same conclusion holds for every test object isomorphic to $C_SL$ with $L\in D^+(S_e,A)$ and is independent of the chosen witness. It is natural in $M,L$ and in identity-normalized changes of factorization that commute with $\Delta$. No adjunction on arbitrary pro-etale objects is asserted.

proof.text: First check the domain of full faithfulness. The closed immersion $c$ is finite, so its etale direct image is exact on abelian sheaves. It is also exact on constant-$A$ modules: kernels, images and cokernels are computed on underlying abelian sheaves, with their induced $A$-actions, and the underlying direct image is the same functor. Open extension $v_{e,!}$ is exact on modules. Hence $\mathcal H^r(F_eL)=v_{e,!}c_{e,*}\mathcal H^r(L)$, by applying these exact functors to kernels and images in a representative complex. Thus $F_eL\in D^+(T_e,A)$. The counit-mate comparison for $c$ is a natural isomorphism on $L\in D^+$; $c$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The open comparison is a natural sheaf isomorphism, hence its degreewise application is a natural isomorphism on complexes and descends to their derived categories. Therefore $\Delta_L$ is a natural isomorphism. The same argument applies with $c,v,L$ replaced by $i,u,L$, giving $E_eL\in D^+$ and invertibility of $B_L$. On the pro-etale site, exactness of closed direct image is the closed case of locally closed extension coherence (take the open factor to be the identity), so the derived direct images in the canonical mate are the displayed termwise closed direct images.

proof.text: Given $h$, compose it with $\Delta_L$ to obtain a morphism $C_TF_eL\to C_TM$. Both $F_eL$ and $M$ are bounded below. Full faithfulness of $C_T$ gives exactly one $h_0:F_eL\to M$ with $C_T(h_0)=h\Delta_L$. Consequently $h=C_T(h_0)\Delta_L^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 099V (lemma-relative-comparison), bounded-below comparison unit; module-coefficient version is the cited node

proof.text:
Put $g_0=\operatorname{adj}_e(h_0)$. The inverse-transpose formula gives $h_0=\epsilon^e_M F_e(g_0)$. Naturality of $\Delta$ at $g_0:L\to H$ gives $F_pC_S(g_0)\Delta_L=\Delta_H C_TF_e(g_0)$. The assumed counit equation therefore yields
$$\begin{aligned}
\epsilon^p_{C_TM}F_p(\gamma_MC_S(g_0))\Delta_L
&=\epsilon^p_{C_TM}F_p(\gamma_M)\Delta_H C_TF_e(g_0)\\
&=C_T(\epsilon^e_M)C_TF_e(g_0)=C_T(h_0)=h\Delta_L.
\end{aligned}$$
Cancel $\Delta_L$. The resulting equality says precisely that the inverse ambient transpose of $\gamma_MC_S(g_0)$ is $h$. Since the transpose is a bijection, $\operatorname{adj}_{F_p\dashv J_p}(h)=\gamma_MC_S(g_0)$.

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), ensuing unit/counit formulas and naturality

proof.text:
Set $z=hq_{p,C_SL}^{-1}$ and $a=h_0q_{e,L}^{-1}:E_eL\to M$. The assumed closure square says $q_{p,C_SL}^{-1}B_L=\Delta_L C_T(q_{e,L}^{-1})$. Thus
$$zB_L=h\Delta_L C_T(q_{e,L}^{-1})=C_T(a).$$
The fixed conjugate identification $J_e\cong s^\times$ identifies the transpose of $a$ under $E_e\dashv s^\times$ with $g_0$: the conjugate is characterized by sending the transpose of $a$ to the transpose of $aq_{e,L}=h_0$. Equivalently its counit square is $\epsilon^E_M E_e(g_0)q_{e,L}=\epsilon^e_M F_e(g_0)=h_0$. This fixes the direction of the conjugate and does not choose a second adjunction structure.

Use the specified formula for $\Phi$ at the closure compactification. By the preceding equality and naturality of the comparison unit,
$$U_T(zB_L)\eta_{T,E_eL}=U_TC_T(a)\eta_{T,E_eL}=\eta_{T,M}a.$$
Naturality of the etale adjunction transpose in its target gives
$$\operatorname{adj}_{E_e\dashv s^\times}(\eta_{T,M}a)
=s^\times(\eta_{T,M})\operatorname{adj}_{E_e\dashv s^\times}(a)
=s^\times(\eta_{T,M})g_0.$$
Apply $C_S$ to obtain $\Phi_{L,C_TM}(z)=\rho_MC_S(g_0)$, as required. Only the displayed normalization of the cited transpose node is used here, not an extension of its Hom bijection to other test objects. The unit $\eta_{T,M}$ is invertible since $M\in D^+$; functors preserve isomorphisms, so $\rho_M=C_Ss^\times(\eta_{T,M})$ is an isomorphism. In particular its target is bounded below, since its source $C_SH$ is.

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), naturality of transpose and of unit; Tag 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints); proetale.tex Tag 099V (lemma-relative-comparison)

proof.text:
Since $\gamma_M$ and $\rho_M$ are isomorphisms, $\theta_M=\rho_M\gamma_M^{-1}$ is an isomorphism, and the two formulas just proved give, for every $h$,
$$\theta_M\operatorname{adj}_{F_p\dashv J_p}(h)
=\Phi_{L,C_TM}(h q_{p,C_SL}^{-1}).$$
This identifies the actual Hom functions, including their inverses. A defined unit is the transpose of the identity on the left-adjoint object, and a defined counit is the inverse transpose of the identity on the right-adjoint object. Evaluating this equality or its inverse on those identities therefore identifies every unit and counit for which the indicated objects belong to the stated domains. In particular $J_pC_TM\cong C_SH$ is an admissible test object, so the counit comparison at $C_TM$ is defined. This argument constructs no unit or counit outside these domains.

proof.text: For a test object $K$ with a witness $\alpha:C_SL\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, transport an arrow $F_pK\to C_TM$ by precomposition with $F_p(\alpha)$, apply the equality of Step 6, and postcompose the resulting source change with $\alpha^{-1}$. This proves the same equality on $K$. For another witness $\beta:C_SL'\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, full faithfulness of $C_S$ lifts $\beta^{-1}\alpha$ uniquely to an isomorphism $t:L\to L'$ (lift its inverse too and use faithfulness on their composites). Naturality in $L$ then identifies the two transported formulas. The comparison-class Hom bijection is itself witness-independent by the cited class-adjunction statement, so this equality is with its specified Hom bijection, rather than a new choice. Naturality in $L$ follows from naturality of $\Delta,q,\Phi$ and the adjunction Hom functions; naturality in $M$ follows in addition from the assumed naturality of $\gamma$ and that of $\eta$.

source.place: Tag 0037 (definition-adjoint), ensuing unit/counit formulas and naturality

proof.text: Finally let $r_\tau:F_\tau\xrightarrow{\sim}F'_\tau$ be an identity-normalized change of factorization with $r_{p,C_SL}\Delta_L=\Delta'_L C_T(r_{e,L})$. For $h'=hr_{p,C_SL}^{-1}$ its etale lift is $h'_0=h_0r_{e,L}^{-1}$, by this equation and uniqueness in Step 2. Conjugation identifies their etale transposes. Let $t:J_p\xrightarrow{\sim}J'_p$ be the corresponding right-adjoint identification (the conjugate of $r_p^{-1}$). Its counit square gives $\operatorname{adj}'_p(h')=t\operatorname{adj}_p(h)$. Apply this to $h=\epsilon^p_{C_TM}F_p(\gamma_M):F_pC_SH\to C_TM$, whose transpose is $\gamma_M$ by Step 3 with $g_0=\mathrm{id}_H$. Its transformed etale lift is the new etale counit under the conjugate identification, so Step 3 for the new factorization gives $\gamma'_M=t\gamma_M$, with the etale right-adjoint identification understood: both sides are the unique transpose of the same normalized counit. The normalized pro-etale closure maps satisfy $q\prime_p r_p=q_p$. Combining this with the two closure squares and $r_p\Delta=\Delta\prime C_T(r_e)$, then cancelling $B$ and using faithfulness of $C_T$, gives $q\prime_e r_e=q_e$ as well. Therefore $h'(q'_{p,C_SL})^{-1}=h q_{p,C_SL}^{-1}$. Hence $\theta'_M t=\theta_M$ under the fixed closure identification. Identity and composition follow from the same equalities and functoriality of conjugation. This proves the asserted factorization naturality under exactly the compatibility stipulated in the item.
